rows.62:5878:
Are you trying to make me angry?
I haven't even told my story yet, and you say I can go home? What is that supposed to mean?
If you say anything that stupid again, I'll kill you.
Hino spent days persuading me before I agreed to come.
Do you intend to let all his trouble go to waste?
He must be so happy to have such a wonderful junior.{p}
rows.62:5b34:
Heh heh...
I knew it.
You seem like that sort.
Aren't you the type who meddles where you're not wanted and tramples into other people's privacy without a second thought?
What a troublesome person.
Well, I suppose it's fine, as long as you enjoy yourself.
But you'd better be very careful.
Nao went through something terrible because of this search.{p}
rows.62:5c74:
He wasn't the type to get a kick out of rumors.
But you see, he just couldn't stop thinking about how the child everyone was talking about had the same name as him.
His classmates said it was probably a coincidence.
But every Sunday, Nao went searching all over for the child's body.{p}
rows.62:5d80:
And he was the very first one to find it.
In a classroom in the old school building.
The wooden floor there has rotted away in places, leaving holes.
The child's body was lying inside one of those holes.
"Aww, you found me."
Suddenly, he heard a voice behind him.{p}
rows.62:5e84:
It was a child with the same face as the body.
Could it be... a ghost...?
He'd never dreamed the story was actually true.
Nao panicked.
But no sound came out of his mouth.
As if he were paralyzed, he couldn't move a single step.
"Now I'm it, mister. It's your turn to hide."
With that, the child melted into the air and vanished.{p}
rows.62:5fac:
At that very moment, the door slammed shut.
It made such a loud noise that it seemed it might break.
Nao ran straight to the door.
But it would not open, no matter what he did.
"Somebody! Somebody!"
He pounded on the door desperately, but no one came.
Just like the child who had died there, he called for help again and again.
...His throat grew raw, and his voice went hoarse.
He felt as if he might start coughing up blood.
But still, no help came.{p}
rows.62:611c:
He couldn't go home that whole night.
Just when he thought he would never get out of there for the rest of his life...{p}
rows.62:6180:
The boy's ghost appeared again.
"You're so noisy, mister, I found you.
That's no good. You're supposed to hide quietly."
And then the door opened.
Nao fled as fast as he could.
He swore he would never go near the old school building again.
As Nao ran, the child murmured at his back,
"Now you're it, mister."{p}Well, {a}?
Do you think Nao took his turn as 'it' and went looking for that child again?
rows.62:62fc: He went looking for the child
rows.62:6314:
Heh heh...
That's right.
There's no reason to go out of your way to see a child like that, is there?
Nao tried to forget all about it.{p}
rows.62:63a4:
...And a few days went by.
His classmates kept up their search as usual.
With all this searching, why hadn't anyone found that classroom?
True, that hole in the floor was dark and hard to spot, but...
Nao found it eerie.
But he couldn't bring himself to tell anyone what he'd been through.
It had all been a bad dream.
Maybe that's what he wanted to believe.{p}
rows.62:6518:
Then one day, that boy appeared before Nao again.
It was during class.
Someone tapped him on the shoulder from behind, and when he turned around, the child was riding on his shoulders.
The child was glaring at Nao with a terrifying look in its eyes.
"Why won't you come look for me?
I've been waiting this whole time.
You're it, mister.
You have to come and find me!"
Nao stared at the child, unable to move.{p}
rows.62:6678:
"Hey, where do you think you're looking?"
The teacher scolded him.
Apparently the teacher couldn't see the child's ghost.
And not only the teacher.
Not one of his classmates could see the child's ghost either.
"H-help me..."
Nao forced the words out.
But everyone laughed.
They thought he had said it because the teacher had scolded him.
Why is everyone laughing?
Don't they care what happens to me?
Unable to bear it any longer, he ran out of the classroom.{p}
rows.62:68a0:
Before he knew it, Nao found himself near the old school building.
No way.
He had no intention of going in there, he thought.
But the ghost's small hands pulled him by the hair and dragged him into the old school building.
Its strength was tremendous.
It was as if the child's obsession were being thrust before his eyes.{p}
rows.62:6a3c:
"I'm getting bored of this game..."
Well, Nao was overjoyed.
Without thinking, he started to smile at it, and the ghost's hand shot out at him.
It was so sudden that Nao couldn't think at all.
He staggered helplessly under the push, and fell into the hole in the floor.{p}
rows.62:6c58:
The next day, he let out the shrillest scream he could, so that someone would hear.
He yelled again and again, over and over.
Even when his voice gave out, he rested only a little, then kept on screaming.
{a}, can you imagine that?
To anyone hearing it from outside, how horrifying that voice must have sounded.
Eventually, a student who heard the screams called a teacher.
Nao was rescued, and he frantically told them everything that had happened.
They say he wept and wailed that he was going to move away somewhere.
And what became of him... can you guess?{p}
rows.62:6e2c:
He got put in a hospital.
People said he must have been wandering around in a daze, fallen into the hole, and hit his head or something.
At first Nao couldn't accept that, but he thought getting away from school wasn't such a bad thing.
He wanted to go somewhere the child's ghost couldn't see him.
For a while, he stayed quietly in the hospital.
But then, two or three days later...{p}
rows.62:6f74:
One night, Nao woke up suddenly and saw someone crouching in a corner of his hospital room.
It was a small child.{p}"Are you sick, mister?"
The voice sounded terribly lonely.
rows.62:7030:
"No... I'm not really sick.
What's the matter with you, kid?
Which room are you from?"
Nao answered timidly.
Could this child be...?
Has the child I met at school followed me here?
With that fear weighing on him, Nao waited for an answer.
"You're not sick?
That's a relief.
But then why did you go home in the middle of hide-and-seek?
I looked for you everywhere!"
When he heard those words, everything went black before Nao's eyes.{p}
rows.62:731c:
...He's in the old school building.
I'm not lying.
I saw the child's ghost dragging Nao there with my own eyes.
When I asked what it was doing, the child smiled sweetly and said they were playing hide-and-seek.{p}
rows.62:73d4:
The child started telling me all about it, having a wonderful time.
How well it had hidden.
How good it was at finding people who hid.
How it had dragged Nao back, even when he'd gone to hide outside the school, and so on.
More or less what I've been telling you.
And Hino saw me then, you see.
He asked me to let him write it up as an article someday.{p}
rows.62:7524:
He calls it an interview, and then holds a get-together like some kind of round-table discussion.
I hate doing things in groups.
So I want no part of this sort of thing.
But Hino is persistent, isn't he?
He kept insisting, so this time I was forced into taking part.
It really puts me in a foul mood.{p}
rows.62:7644:
Oh, yes. It seems Nao was taken to the classroom where the child died.
Inside the hole in that classroom's floor, the two Naos must be getting along nicely.
One in the form of a child.
The other in the form of a high school student.
It seems the two of them having the same name was pure coincidence.
The one to pity is the high school Nao.
He was never the type to stick his nose into strange rumors to begin with...{p}
rows.62:7790:
If anything, {a}, isn't it people like you, who get a kick out of rumors, who ought to meet that kind of fate?
Heh heh...
Go to the old school building sometime, if you feel like it.
The two Naos might let you join their game of hide-and-seek.{p}...That's the end of my story.
Now, the fifth one is next.
What kind of story will you tell us this time?{p}
rows.62:78b4:
Heh heh...
Does that mean that's what you would do?
Oh, please. If you did that, you would have to play hide-and-seek with the child's ghost forever.
That might be fine for you, but Nao thought differently.
He tried to forget all about it.{p}
rows.62:7a0c:
"You know, I used to hurt all over, and get hungry, but now I'm fine.
Hey, mister, you should become just like me."
The child's cold hand touched Nao.
"Then we can play hide-and-seek together forever..."{p}
rows.62:7af4:
...They say that the next day, Nao was found dead in his hospital room.
Apparently there was quite a fuss over it, with talk of psychological shock.
The truth is, Nao had an older brother who went missing as a small child.
Supposedly he went out to play one day and never came back...{p}
rows.62:7bfc:
The child's body in the old school building belonged to that older brother.
After losing their child, the parents gave Nao, who was born later, the same name as his brother.
That's why Nao and the child's ghost had the same name.
The child's ghost knew that, and that's why it kept haunting Nao.
Its own little brother, all grown up...{p}
rows.62:7d1c:
I wonder what the brother was thinking when he met Nao in the form of a child.
Didn't it occur to him that if he killed his little brother, their parents and Nao's friends would grieve?
...Maybe he just couldn't think that far.
Maybe that child only wanted to be with the little brother he'd met by chance.{p}
rows.62:7e3c:
You see, after the incident, I met the child's ghost in the old school building.
That's when I heard the story I just told you, but...
Hino happened to pass by.
He said he wanted me to let him write it up as an article someday.
Back then, Hino was new to the newspaper club, and he had no say in anything.
I figured he wouldn't be able to do much of an interview anyway, so I just gave him some offhand answer.
Who would have thought he'd end up setting up a gathering like this?
You never can tell.{p}...Well, that's the end of my story.
Next is the fifth story.
Who will be telling it this time, I wonder?{p}
rows.62:8018:
Oh my.
{a}, you're in the newspaper club, aren't you?
Is that really good enough?
If you don't keep your antennae up for all sorts of things, you'll never write a good article.
Well, whatever kind of article you write makes no difference to me.{p}
rows.62:816c:
No, that's not right.
After all, the students had all been searching mainly around the old school building.{p}
rows.62:81b8:
You really are a tiring person.
Your sense of things seems a little off from normal people's.
I thought there was something odd about Nao.
But I never told anyone about it.{p}
rows.62:8260: I wonder what way of thinking leads you to that.{p}
rows.62:8290:
People like that are exactly the ones spirits find easiest to latch onto.
Wouldn't you be better off dropping that half-hearted sympathy?
But I'll tell you about the child later.
First, Nao's story.{p}
rows.62:8324:
I see...
Well, people feel all sorts of ways about things.
I'll tell you about the child in detail later.
First, Nao's story.{p}
rows.62:8394:
I see...
And here I was, going to the trouble of telling you.
But maybe it's better that you don't hear it.
It's a rather nasty story.
It might not be suitable for a school article anyway.
Well then, let's end my story here.{p}
rows.62:848c:
...What?
You want to ask about what I said at the beginning?
Oh, you mean how I ended up having to come here because Hino saw me talking with that child?
...Too bad, but I can't explain that without first telling you why the child was killed.{p}So that's the end of my story.
Whose turn is next, I wonder?{p}
rows.62:85ac:
Oh my.
You say the same thing Nao did.{p}
rows.62:85e0:
He told me,
"Why don't we keep this a secret?"
Just like that.
"Let's not tell anyone that the year head killed that child, either.
I mean, think how awful it would be for the mother.
Her child murdered, and her husband a criminal..."
I had no particular intention of making it public either.
It would just be a bother.
It had nothing to do with me.
Just as I was about to tell him that was fine by me, he started saying something.{p}
rows.62:8758:
I see...
I didn't know either.{p}
